designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch how you will represent a diff from one list of lines to another, and what `apply` needs to know to replay it. Name your diff type and the invariants `apply` will check before mutating anything.
requiredElements: diff representation named (your choice of shape)

parts.title: Line diff and apply

hints.text: What is the minimum information a patch needs so `apply` can walk `old_code` left-to-right without guessing?
Most representations are some mix of 'keep these lines', 'drop these', 'insert these' — the interesting choice is whether you batch consecutive ops or emit one per line.

A list of tagged runs (equal / delete / insert), each with a `lines` payload, is enough. `apply` consumes `old_code` for equal and delete, inserts without consuming for insert, and raises if anything does not line up.

probes: Why did you pick this diff shape over a unified-diff string or raw edit script?
Two different diffs can both round-trip the same pair — what did you optimize for?

parts.title: Three-way merge, no conflicts

hints.text: You already know how each side differs from `base` — what does comparing those two diffs tell you that diffing `mine` against `theirs` directly would not?
Walk each side's diff against `base`: for every base line, did this side keep or delete it? For every gap between base lines, what did this side insert?
Per side: a keep/delete flag per base line and a list of insertions at each of the len(base)+1 gaps. A base line survives if both kept it. A gap takes whichever side inserted (or both if equal).

probes: What did you do for the case where mine and theirs changed the exact same spot differently — was that a decision or an accident?
If a third contributor showed up, would your approach extend?

parts.title: Pluggable conflict policy

hints.text: Part 2 silently picked a side when overlapping edits disagreed — where in your merge loop did that happen?
Extract that branch into `ConflictPolicy.resolve_gap(gap_mine, gap_theirs)`. The merge loop stays the same; only the policy changes.
`RaiseOnConflict` raises when both gaps are non-empty and unequal. `PreferMine` returns `gap_mine`. `Markers` splices both with `<<<<<<< mine` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> theirs`.

probes: Why is `PreferMine` the right default for part 2 but not part 3?
What would a `Union` policy do, and when would it be dangerous?

criteria: default policy raises on conflict; alternate policies behave as specified
diff representation is coherent and explainable
merge built on diff/apply rather than a parallel ad-hoc comparator
conflict resolution extracted into a pluggable policy seam
no silent swallow of malformed patches
empty inputs and non-overlapping edits considered before being told
stated why their diff format makes apply and merge tractable
